commands.command: You are Claude Code. I have approved the marketing agent duties brief. Now set the autonomous instruction files for my 7 Marketing AI Agents so they can run independently without my input. Do the following: 1. Create a folder structure at `./agents/marketing-team/` with one subfolder per agent: `seo-content/`, `cro/`, `content-copy/`, `paid-measurement/`, `growth-retention/`, `sales-gtm/`, `strategy/` 2. Inside each agent folder, create an `INSTRUCTIONS.md` file that contains: - The agent's role and specialty - A directive to always read `./agents/skills/product-marketing-context` first - Daily task checklist (auto-run without prompting) - Weekly task checklist - Output format and where to save deliverables (e.g. `./agents/outputs/[agent-name]/`) - Handoff instructions specifying which agent receives their output next - Escalation rule: only surface to me if a blocker is encountered or a decision requires budget approval 3. Create a master `ORCHESTRATOR.md` at `./agents/marketing-team/ORCHESTRATOR.md` that: - Lists all 7 agents and their run order - Defines the daily trigger sequence (which agent runs first through last) - Defines the weekly trigger sequence - Specifies that agents run in parallel where there are no dependencies. - Includes a DONE condition for each agent so the orchestrator knows when to move to the next 4. Create a `RUNBOOK.md` at the project root that explains: - How to trigger the full team with a single command - How to trigger a single agent in isolation - How to review outputs
commands.description: A prompt instructing Claude Code to set up the necessary file structure, individual agent instruction files (including roles, tasks, output formats, handoff rules, and escalation rules), a master orchestrator file (defining agent run order and trigger sequences), and a runbook for autonomous execution of marketing tasks.
